title: Approximate SMT Counting Beyond Discrete Domains
problem: Satisfiability Modulo Theory (SMT) solvers handle complex hybrid formulas with discrete and continuous variables, but extending them to model counting—especially for discrete projections in hybrid formulas—is challenging; existing methods like bit-blasting cannot handle continuous variables.
motivation: Model counting capabilities in SMT extend automated reasoning for hybrid systems (control, cyber-physical, design verification); existing discrete-only approaches miss hybrid applications.
method: pact is an SMT model counter using hashing-based approximate model counting with theoretical error guarantees. It makes logarithmic SMT solver calls relative to projection variables, using optimized hash functions to partition solution spaces and approximate discrete projections in hybrid formulas.
key_novelty: Hashing-based approximate SMT model counting with logarithmic solver query complexity for hybrid formulas with continuous domains.
contributions: First SMT model counter for hybrid formulas with continuous and discrete variables
Hashing-based approximate counting with theoretical guarantees
Logarithmic SMT solver complexity in projection variable count
Significant performance on large benchmark suites (603 of 14,202 instances solved vs. 13 for baseline)

metrics.other: logarithmic query complexity in projection variables

baselines: prior SMT solvers and model counting approaches
limitations: Solution quality and error bounds not fully characterized; scalability to very large hybrid formulas (millions of variables) not discussed.
primary_theme: hashing-based approximate SMT model counting for hybrid formulas
